title: Implement N-Queens solver in Rust
description: Implement solve_n_queens(n: usize) -> usize that counts distinct valid arrangements of N non-attacking queens on an N×N board using backtracking.

task_spec.prompt:
Implement solve_n_queens via backtracking in src/lib.rs:
- Helper fn backtrack(board: &mut Vec<usize>, row: usize, n: usize) -> usize
- Base case: if row == n return 1
- For each col 0..n: if is_safe(board, row, col), set board[row]=col, recurse, add result
- fn is_safe(board: &[usize], row: usize, col: usize): for each r in 0..row, check board[r]!=col and |board[r]-col|!=|r-row| (diagonals)
- solve_n_queens creates the board and calls backtrack
All 4 cargo test cases must pass.
followup_prompts: Run `cargo test --quiet` and show me which tests are passing and which are still failing. Fix any failures — pay attention to edge cases like empty input, boundary values, and error conditions.
Final check: run `cargo test --quiet` one more time. All tests must be green. If anything is still failing, trace through the failing assertion and fix it now.
